newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serbs say OSCE will judge fairness of elections.
newsitem.headline: Serbs say OSCE will judge fairness of elections.

text.p: A senior Bosnian Serb official said on Sunday the international commnunity and not the main Moslem political party should decide whether the country's elections were legitimate.
"It is not the Moslems who are the judges and planners of these elections and thank God for that," Jovan Zametica, advisor to acting Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic, told reporters.
"We have the international community here. We have the OSCE and they will be the judges of these elections."

Zametica spoke a day after Bosnian president Alija Izetbegovic warned that the Moslem-led government would not recognise the results of Saturday's elections in Serb territory because of alleged irregularities.

The post-war elections, which are supposed to establish joint institutions governing a union of Serb and Moslem-Croat entities, were deemed a success by organisers from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission in Bosnia.

Prior to Saturday's poll, human rights workers reported Serb authorities coerced many refugees to registering in towns conquered by Bosnian Serb forces instead of their pre-war homes in the Moslem-Croat Federation.

Registration abuses led the OSCE to postpone the municipal elections but officials decided to go ahead with general elections as scheduled on Saturday, saying the delay would jeopardise the fragile peace process.
"I think it's not surprising that the Moslem leadership is crying foul play," Zametica said.
As the largest national group in Bosnia, the Moslems "have always tried to dominate it," said Zametica, a long-time aide to hard-line nationalist leader Radovan Karadzic.
Indicted by the UN War Crimes Tribunal, Karadzic stepped down as Bosnian Serb president in July to enable his Serb Democratic Party (SDS) to stand in the elections.
The SDS led a campaign to carve out a separate state in Bosnia by expelling Moslems and Croats froim conquered territory during three and a half years of war.
SDS officials have taken pains to cooperate with OSCE organisers as they believe the elections will help seal the ethnic division of Bosnia to legalise the Serb Republic as a separate state.
Zametica said he believed the major powers would certify the election results and called on the main Moslem Party for Democratic Action (SDA) to drop their objection.
"Let's hope that wiser council prevails and that we are heading for a period of peace and prosperity."
